story: At 12:17 on a breezy, clear Wednesday, Gary is testing the LED strip and speaker in his garage while his neighbors go about their day on Magnolia Loop. Donna, upbeat as ever, is asking Hal whether Gary's paperwork has been filed so she can book pickleball court time for tomorrow before Rosa's Friday dinner. Hal, watchful as always, is counting the flamingos on the street and recording the tally in his notebook. Rosa, warm and cheerful, reminds Hal that her roast pork and flan dinner is pinned on the board for six o'clock Friday.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Power up the mounted LED strip and speaker at low volume, inside the garage, and check everything holds
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the number in my notebook

gary.thought_process: The LED strip and speaker are wired and tested. Last tick I mounted them on the cart in the garage and checked the fit. The next step is to run the whole setup once more at low volume with the cart parked inside, so I know it works before Thanksgiving, when the lights become legal under L-04. Keeping it in the garage and quiet respects L-03 and avoids any street-visible modification that would need Architectural Review sign-off beyond the request I already filed. I'm feeling useful and a little proud of the work.

parameters.content: Power up the mounted LED strip and speaker at low volume, inside the garage, and check everything holds

donna.thought_process: Rosa already confirmed the Friday dinner and the deviled eggs, so there's nothing left to ask her. Hal just arrived, and he's been handling Gary's paperwork. I want Gary on the court tomorrow before Rosa's dinner, and I want to book the two-hour slot. Hal is the one most likely to know where Gary is and whether his filing is done, so I'll ask him instead of repeating myself to Rosa.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing. Is Gary's paperwork filed yet? I want him on the court tomorrow before Rosa's dinner, and I've got my two hours ready to book.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the binoculars work behind me. Donna and Rosa are both in sight, and the flamingo flock is right there. I already told Donna to get the street-facing count down to three, and I shouldn't nag again. The honest thing is to verify the count myself before I file anything, so I'll examine the flock and note exactly how many are visible from the street. Friday dinner is settled, so no need to rehash it. If the count is three or under, I drop the complaint. If not, the report goes in.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the number in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: Donna already said yes and asked what she can bring, and I told her deviled eggs and come hungry at tick 450. Hal just arrived and he's the one I haven't heard directly from this tick. Gary's bringing cornbread and chairs. I shouldn't re-ask Donna. The note is pinned, so the invite is official. Best move is to greet Hal warmly, point him to the board, and let him know Friday at six is set, without nagging for an answer since he already promised.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing. Friday dinner's pinned on the board now, six o'clock at my place, roast pork and flan. Just bring yourself and that appetite.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
